conditions: A new or materially changed realisation boundary is governed by a tier-3 DESIGN_MODULE design profile.
concepts.definition: The canonical design-to-module evidence route comprises semantic derivation from constitutional WHAT and owning requirements through accepted ontology, declared carrier inventory, target design and domain/sequence/state evidence to implementation and module-derived unit tests, reconciliation and acceptance, then promotion and design-method closure. A distinct feedback chain carries implementation/test evidence, counterexamples or falsification to affected ontology or design relations.

grounding.quote:
constitutional WHAT and owning requirements
  -> accepted ontology, the carrier inventory the design declares,
     target design, and the design's domain, sequence and state evidence
  -> implementation and module-derived unit tests
  -> reconciliation and acceptance
  -> promotion and design-method closure

implementation and module-derived unit tests
  -> evidence, counterexample or falsification input
  -> affected ontology or design relation

concepts.label: Design-to-module evidence route

conditions: Within the design-profile evidence route.
concepts.definition: The accepted ontology, declared carrier inventory, target design, domain/sequence/state evidence and module boundary assets provide the semantic and structural design basis. The module boundary is an intermediate ownership-based reasoning surface subordinate to constitutional truth and ratified design.

grounding.quote:
The module boundary is the intermediate reasoning surface
that lets implementation and unit tests be audited against the same
ownership cut; it does not outrank constitutional truth or ratified design
(P6).

concepts.label: Design and module ownership basis

concepts.definition: Implementation and module-derived unit tests are downstream realisation artifacts and sources of execution evidence, counterexamples and falsification input; they do not thereby acquire semantic selection or acceptance authority.

grounding.quote:
implementation and module-derived unit tests
  -> evidence, counterexample or falsification input
  -> affected ontology or design relation
```

The first chain is semantic derivation. The second is evidence feedback
and cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer (P6).

concepts.label: Implementation and unit-test evidence

conditions: Within the product-assurance bounded context and under the design profile.
concepts.definition: Module-derived unit tests are module-owned proof lanes derived from realisation authority owned by DESIGN_MODULE. Product-level UAT and acceptance meaning remain with Product authority. Integration, scenario and sandbox lanes are broader downstream proof families.

grounding.quote:
Within the product-assurance bounded context of §2, the two authority
sources stay distinct: the module-derived unit test and its proof relation
derive from realisation authority, which the design profile owns
(DESIGN_MODULE), and this section states that relation so both sources sit
in one member; that ownership does not extend to Product-level UAT or
acceptance meaning, which stays with Product authority under §2 (P6;
provenance rc.2 DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #6b-module-derived-unit-test-rule).

Unit tests under the design profile are module-owned proof lanes.

concepts.label: Module-derived unit proof

conditions: Under the design profile.
concepts.definition: Lifecycle confirmation covers every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface and published profile function or module. It consumes SPEC_METHOD §2's operational lifecycle chain without redefining phases and detects ambiguity about ultimate intended use; it is neither a release plan nor a replacement for RELEASE.

grounding.quote:
Every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface,
plugin surface, public interface, data surface, and published function or
module of a profile exists inside an operational lifecycle. Under the
design profile that lifecycle signal is confirmed at the realisation
boundary before design-method closure (P2, P6; provenance rc.2
DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #6c-module-lifecycle-confirmation-rule). The
canonical operational lifecycle chain is SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational
lifecycle sufficiency; this section consumes that chain and does not
redefine its phases. The checklist is not a release plan and does not
replace RELEASE; it is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.

concepts.label: Module lifecycle confirmation

concepts.definition: ASSURANCE's source-disposition ledger records predecessor anchors, successor loci and claimed conservation or change. Its three tables concern rc.2 SPEC_METHOD, STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE and DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD. Routes are provenance only. Profile generalisations are Ontology→ontology; IACS→declared carrier inventory; three-view evidence→domain/sequence/state evidence; co_evolution_admissible(B)→design co-evolution condition; decision_complete(B)→decision-complete; graph function/GTL module→published profile function/module; this method→design profile; agentic execution relation→ACTIVATION §1; RELEASE_METHOD→RELEASE. DESIGN_MODULE owns bindings. Predecessor must becomes indicative; should, may and minimum retain force.

grounding.quote:
Every row is restated in this member's own text; a route is
provenance only.

concepts.label: Assurance source-disposition ledger

concepts.definition: The subject's Tier-1 STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, a_c, is a domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus. Its stable concept identity is urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c, owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus. It owns theory, signature, typed records, AC-001–AC-020, traversals, functor kinds, interpretation, models, layers, identity, application/import boundaries, exclusions and conformance obligations. It consumes rather than redefines FOUNDATIONS ontology and core result algebra.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns the a_c theory in full: position and scope, the signature,
the typed records, the laws AC-001 to AC-020, traversals and functor
kinds, interpretation and models, the three governed layers, the law of
calculus identity, the application boundary, external imports, exclusions
and the conformance obligations of this member.

Its stable
concept identity is `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. This member
owns that concept in the bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are
declared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory
that publishes them (P3; rc.2 #position).

concepts.label: Subject a_c calculus

concepts.definition: The derivation account links nine recurring commitments to current owners and rc.2 clause families: scoped identity/authority conservation (FOUNDATIONS §2; IDENTITY_METHOD core-law and UP-004); bounded-context meaning (FOUNDATIONS §2; SPEC_METHOD semantic resolution); bounded probabilistic construction (P0, FOUNDATIONS §2, ACTIVATION §1; REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD position/evaluation); delegated construction and assessment separation (ACTIVATION §1, EVALUATION §3; SPEC_METHOD UP-020); ambiguity and human adjudication/hard stops (ACTIVATION §4; SPEC_METHOD ambiguity governance); exact-basis/evidence-verdict separation and closed results (RF-005/006/007 and FOUNDATIONS §4 restating RF-012); constitutional derivation/re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §1/§4); finite closure/projection/residuals/capability fit (REFERENCE_FRAME §3, AC-010/011); singular released authority (SPEC_METHOD §6, PRODUCT_DEFINITION activation). These are provenance accounts, not imported normative definitions.

grounding.quote:
These references establish provenance. The definitions and laws of this
member are the sole normative authority for the meaning of `a_c` within
the selected complete cut. A consumer needs no implicit representation of
the method, no particular carrier and no downstream implementation to
interpret the calculus (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Calculus derivation account

concepts.definition: Material family F9's foundation-to-law table distinguishes premises, consequences, added choices and their owners. Its instance premises are finite model representation, separately identified exact subject/model/optional carrier, and mechanically decidable versus probabilistic or human predicates. P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 are marked independent; P0 recovered; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. The table maps these to position, scope, signature/reference closure, identity/typing, authority/basis, result/refusal, latitude, residuals, closure/projection, overlay, transformation, judgment separation, traversal/composition, interpretation/validity, layers, edition identity, application boundaries, constraint surfaces and conformance. Added choices remain owned: calculus names/core shapes/refusal precedence/canonicalisation/minimum conformance by this member; domains and contracts by signatures; latitude, overlays, transformations and composites by their named owners; semantic acceptance and downstream products by downstream authorities; task seeds/relations by activation.

grounding.quote:
Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others
  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.

concepts.label: Foundation-to-law and consumer map

concepts.definition: Sigma = (RecordKind, Sort, RelationKind, ConstraintKind, ResidualKind, FunctorKind, JudgmentKind, StopKind). Each member is a finite closed identity set for one model family. The eight fixed record-kind URNs share prefix urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind: and suffixes semantic-object, typed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation, judgment. The signature defines every record/sort field and value domain, identity-reference cardinality/domain, relation endpoint sorts, constraint subjects/predicates, residual subject/uncertainty/consequence/re-entry domains, judgment input/output/evidence/stops and permitted traversal functor kinds.

grounding.quote:
RecordKind_ac = {
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment
}

concepts.label: Closed calculus signature

concepts.definition: M_b = (b,I,O,E,C,L,X,V,T,J): exact basis; closed identity universe; finite semantic-object, directed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation and judgment populations. Population_M maps each fixed record kind to its corresponding population. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind,field) specifies cardinality, allowed local record kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population
is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and
record identities are unique across their disjoint union.

concepts.label: Exact-basis model and populations

concepts.definition: SemanticObject has exactly id, sort, context, owner, scope, basis, value. Id, sort, context, owner and basis are identities; scope is the closed governed domain; value is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or an exact-content reference. Id, owner and sort carry scoped Object identity; scope carries its boundary.

grounding.quote:
`id`, `sort`, `context`, `owner` and `basis` are identities. `scope` is
the closed governed domain. `value` is sort-defined carrier-neutral content
or a reference to exact content. A semantic object is an Object of
FOUNDATIONS §2 whose scoped identity is carried by `id`, `owner` and
`sort` and whose boundary is `scope`.

concepts.label: SemanticObject record

concepts.definition: TypedRelation has exactly id, kind, source, target, context, owner, scope, basis, qualifiers. Endpoints resolve in I. Qualifiers are a closed kind-specific record of signature-required direction, cardinality, preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics.

grounding.quote:
`source` and `target` resolve to members of `I`. `qualifiers` is the
closed kind-specific record declaring direction, cardinality,
preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics
required by the signature.

concepts.label: TypedRelation record

concepts.definition: Constraint has exactly id, kind, applies_to, predicate, context, owner, scope, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref, refusal. Kind and judgment_kind resolve declared ConstraintKind and JudgmentKind identities. The signature owns predicate language and judgment semantics.

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves
one declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate
language and how its result is judged.

concepts.label: Constraint record

concepts.definition: Latitude is an explicit permission set within a constraint boundary, with exactly id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis, invalidation.

grounding.quote:
Latitude = {
  id,
  applies_to,
  allowed_variation,
  forbidden_variation,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  invalidation
}

concepts.label: Latitude record

concepts.definition: Residual uncertainty is first-class model content. Residual has exactly id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry, invalidation. Its kind resolves one declared ResidualKind; the signature defines all lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains.

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines
its lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation
domains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission
(P3).

concepts.label: Residual record

concepts.definition: AC-001–AC-020 govern signature, typed and traversal records and the FOUNDATIONS ontology. Identity, authority, basis and residual definitions remain owned by FOUNDATIONS; the calculus owns these laws over them.

grounding.quote:
The objects these laws govern are the records of §2, §3 and §5 and the
ontology of FOUNDATIONS §2; where a law names identity, authority, basis
or residual, the definition is FOUNDATIONS' and the law is this member's.

concepts.label: Fundamental calculus laws

concepts.definition: Constraint judgments and calculus operation outcomes map to the existing core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, for their own named predicates. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis); refusal causes are part of their values. Missing judgments and unapplied operations have no result.

grounding.quote:
This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

concepts.label: Core results and cause-specific stops

concepts.definition: For model M, seed Z and exact dependency relation family R, closure_R(M,Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M,Q)). This is least lawful record closure under R, not globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.

grounding.quote: closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q))

concepts.label: Material closure

concepts.definition: Projection selects meaning-preserving model views: project(M,Z,R) returns (M_Z,Boundary_Z), gap or refusal. M_Z contains Z's material closure; Boundary_Z records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A projection is a reference, not a new semantic owner.

grounding.quote:
`M_Z` contains the material closure of `Z`, so a projection's `gap` or
`refusal` is that of the closure it contains or of the model it acts on:
`gap` or `refusal(basis)` (AC-007). `Boundary_Z` records excluded,
external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A
projection is not a new semantic owner.

concepts.label: Model projection

concepts.definition: An overlay adds explicit records to one or more declared Population_M families of a basis model without mutating that basis.

grounding.quote:
An overlay adds explicit records to one or more declared `Population_M`
families of a basis model. It does not mutate the basis.

concepts.label: Model overlay

concepts.definition: Transformation is an operation-bearing specialisation of one exact traversal. Its fields are id, traversal, domain_model, codomain_model, context, owner, scope, basis, operation_authority, preconditions, preservation_relation, preserved, introduced, removed, external_preserved, external_introduced, external_removed, external_resolution_witnesses, residuals, evidence, provenance, stop_states, invalidation, re_entry. T[t](M_b,inputs) returns proposed M_b_prime*, hold, gap or refusal while leaving the input unchanged.

grounding.quote:
A transformation is an operation-bearing specialisation of one exact
traversal record `v` (§5).

concepts.label: Transformation contract

concepts.definition: Judgment is a record pointing to an unchanged subject, with exactly id, kind, subject, subject_digest, context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance, decided_at.

grounding.quote:
Judgment = {
  id,
  kind,
  subject,
  subject_digest,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  evaluator,
  authority,
  decision,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  decided_at
}

concepts.label: Judgment record concept

concepts.definition: A traversal is a typed contract with id, domain, codomain, context, owner, scope, basis, preconditions, postconditions, authority, evidence, provenance, stop_states. Application F_K[v](X_v) returns Y_v or its closed stop algebra Omega_v, binding one exact traversal and one functor kind.

grounding.quote:
where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra.

concepts.label: Traversal contract

concepts.definition: Three generic functor kinds have identities urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d, :f-p and :f-h. F_D is deterministic evaluation/proof returning judgment without constructing the domain object judged; F_P is bounded probabilistic interpretation/construction/proposal under an exact traversal, without authority from usefulness or repeatability; F_H is explicit human adjudication under exact identity, authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Actor, executor, domain operation and functor kind are distinct coordinates.

grounding.quote:
The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Generic functor classifications

concepts.definition: Interpret_a_c(subject_basis,signature,interpretation_contract) returns proposed M_subject*, hold, gap or refusal. The contract binds exact calculus basis; subject identity, inventory and bytes/semantic addresses; signature and compatible extension; mappings into every applicable population; interpreter identity/capability/provenance/stops; structural evaluation contract; semantic selection and acceptance authority; source re-entry and invalidation rules. The star marks absence of applicable semantic acceptance.

grounding.quote:
The trailing `*` marks a proposed model that has not
received the
applicable semantic acceptance judgment. The interpretation contract is
the Interpretation of FOUNDATIONS §2 made exact for one subject and one
signature.

concepts.label: Subject interpretation contract

concepts.definition: a_c.X is exact subject X interpreted as a calculus model, independently identified from pure calculus and carrier. Its identity binds exact calculus identity, exact subject basis, interpretation contract, selected model-content identity and semantic-selection ledger identity/digest. An accepted interpretation is the pair (a_c.X,J_X), with J_X external to its subject identity.

grounding.quote:
a_c       = the pure calculus
a_c.X     = subject X interpreted as a model of a_c
a_c.X.C   = that accepted model encoded in carrier C

concepts.label: Interpreted model layer

conditions: The model has applicable accepted semantic judgment.
concepts.definition: a_c.X.C is that accepted model encoded in carrier C. Its identity binds exact interpreted-model identity, exact carrier Product/cut, exact encoding profile and canonical carrier-content identity. Admitted encoding is the triple (a_c.X.C,J_X,D_C), with external semantic-acceptance and carrier-admission judgments.

grounding.quote:
The admitted encoding evidence relation is the exact
triple `(G_C, J_X, D_C)`; neither judgment enters the identity of its
subject (P6, P3).

concepts.label: Encoded carrier layer

concepts.definition: AxiomaticCalculusBasis is an external edition record created after publication bytes exist: kind stdo.axiomatic-calculus-basis; schema_version 1; fixed calculus concept_identity; derivation_basis containing immutable absolute predecessor release_uri, sha256-prefixed 64-lowercase-hex manifest_sha256 and nonempty absolute semantic-address principle_refs; publication_basis containing distinct immutable absolute successor release_uri, manifest_sha256, member_uri inside that release and member_sha256. Identity is urn:stdo:axiomatic-calculus-basis:sha256: concatenated with sha256(JCS(record)).

grounding.quote:
The stable concept identity does not identify one immutable calculus
edition. An exact released calculus basis is an external record created
after the publication bytes exist. It keeps the predecessor authority from
which the edition was derived distinct from the successor carrier that
publishes it (P3, P6; rc.2 #exact-calculus-identity):

concepts.label: Released calculus basis identity

conditions: A declared subject and work boundary select exact task seeds Z and dependency family R.
concepts.definition: A constraint surface is project(M_subject,Z,R) over material closure: objects/meanings, predicates/dependencies, admissible operations, required results, latitude, retained authority, evidence and unresolved conditions/seams. Shared premises remain single records; closure imposes neither tree shape nor execution order. It constrains obligations without prescribing internal solution strategy beyond them.

grounding.quote:
A constraint surface states, for a declared subject and work boundary,
the obligations and the permitted freedom of the work: its objects and
their meanings, the predicates and dependencies that bear on it, the
admissible operations, the required results, the authority, the evidence
and the conditions still unresolved. It constrains the work without
prescribing the worker's internal solution strategy beyond those
obligations (P2, P6).

concepts.label: Task constraint surface

concepts.definition: The calculus source-disposition ledger routes every listed rc.2 clause to successor sections and records conservation, generalisation, correction and new law. It claims no authority from provenance routes. New/tightened matters include F9's table; resolved derivation addresses placed in principle_refs rather than release_uri; result and cause-specific stop mappings and refusal precedence; unresolved-resolution gap versus dangling-reference refusal; stop refinements preserving parent core values; explicit traversal ownership and missing-traversal refusal; layer judgment mappings; release-time identity issuance; and new constraint-surface law. Graph/profile-specific wording is generalised without claimed loss.

grounding.quote:
Rows received by this member. Anchors are into rc.2
AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md; a locus is a section of this file unless another
member is named. Every row is restated in this member's own text; a route
is provenance only.

concepts.label: Calculus source-disposition ledger

concepts.definition: Tier-2 CONFORMANCE owns corpus qualification cases (§1–§4) and a common-discriminator qualification map (§5). A discriminator is a situation whose expected distinction separates conforming from defective corpora. The external construction specification owns expected distinctions. Cases name subject, mechanism, independently specified expected distinction and status. Status records an existing fixture, fresh-constructor runs or independent assessment; status is not a result and a run is not a pass.

grounding.quote:
A case names its subject, the mechanism under test, the independently
specified expected distinction, and its status. A status names what
exists: a fixture designed, runs by a fresh constructor, or an assessment
by an independent assessor under EVALUATION §3 and §7. A status is a record
of what exists, not a result. A run is not a pass; only an assessment
records one.

concepts.label: Corpus qualification cases and discriminator map

concepts.definition: Twelve reported historical failure classes from building with rc.2 and predecessors form planned cases C-01–C-12. Every supplied case has status not run; their expected distinctions are prospective assessment criteria, not observed passes.

grounding.quote:
These are failure classes observed while building with the rc.2 method and
its predecessors, as reported in the common inputs. Each names the mechanism
that must catch it.

concepts.label: Historical counterexample case set

conditions: The design-profile route applies.
exceptions: Co-evolution is permitted only when the design's co-evolution condition holds.
An unchanged realization_refactor cites the accepted relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta instead of recreating evidence.

grounding.quote:
Where the design is not decision-complete, the relation is
design-gated at the smallest causally closed affected decision set and
retained implementation follows its acceptance.

constraints.statement: Expected results retain assertion provenance from semantic derivation and executions retain execution provenance from feedback. Agreement can share an error; disagreement requires diagnosis. Feedback cannot select or accept semantic answers. Design retains structural HOW, including during co-evolution. If decision-incomplete, acceptance of the smallest causally closed affected decision set gates retained implementation.
constraints.uncertainty: The co-evolution predicate and change-class definition are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: Construction is probabilistic or agentic.

grounding.quote:
The design profile supplies the governing-frame,
transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction,
computational-realisation and module evidence that relation consumes; it
does not define a second execution protocol (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: ACTIVATION §1 governs the accepted-design handoff into bounded construction, assessment, disposition, checkpoint and continuation. The profile supplies governing-frame, transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction, computational-realisation and module evidence; it defines no second execution protocol.

conditions: Claiming design-method evidence completeness, promotion or closure.

grounding.quote:
- the final implementation is traceable to the accepted ontology;
- the final implementation is traceable to design and module boundary
  assets;
- unit tests are traceable to module ownership, not only to helper
  layout;
- implementation-first discoveries are reconciled into the ontology and
  the design's domain, sequence and state evidence before promotion or
  closure; and
- implementation may not compensate for an unrealised declared
  constructor by introducing a hidden controller or alternative authority
  path.

constraints.statement: Final implementation must trace to accepted ontology and design/module assets; tests trace to module ownership beyond helper layout; implementation-first discoveries must be reconciled into ontology and domain/sequence/state evidence before promotion or closure. No hidden controller or alternative authority path may compensate for an unrealised declared constructor. Tests discovered from implementation must have closure proof re-expressed against module ownership. A design/code-to-tests jump without module-boundary reconstruction has too weak a proof surface.

exceptions: Where a reference realisation exists, use the reference-specific chain.

grounding.quote: The minimum complete evidence chain is (P6, P4b):

constraints.statement: Minimum ordered chain: constitutional WHAT; accepted ontology; target design; target module assets and ontology-derived carrier inventory; accepted domain/sequence/state projections with axiom evaluation; implementation; unit tests derived from the same ontology and module boundary. With a reference realisation: constitutional WHAT; reference design; accepted target ontology and reference-to-ontology mapping; target design mapping; target module assets and ontology-derived carrier inventory; accepted domain/sequence/state projections with axiom evaluation; implementation and tests derived from the same ontology.

conditions: Unit tests are under the design profile.
exceptions: Helper-level tests are permitted, but cannot be the canonical module-boundary proof surface.
Transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but cannot replace module-derived unit proof.

grounding.quote:
If a module has code but no
module-derived unit test lane, the module is not closure-ready under the
design profile.

constraints.statement: Tests derive from module ownership, not code shape alone. They should trace to accepted ontology and applicable entity/lifecycle/authority/function/effect/projection law; governing module design; active declared or equivalent carrier inventory; module-bounded domain/sequence/state projections; and owned requirement families. They are not primarily authored from helper boundaries, private-method layout, incidental branches, temporary decomposition or mock convenience hiding the contract. The required question is what the module owns and what proof that ownership requires. Module-owned unit tests are authoritative for module proof; broader integration/scenario/sandbox lanes remain downstream. Code without a module-derived unit lane is not closure-ready.
constraints.uncertainty: ASSURANCE §7's exact unit-frame claims and non-closure boundaries are not supplied.

conditions: For every governed boundary, before design-method closure.

grounding.quote:
For each governed boundary, the design evidence states, or points to a
surface that states (P6, P5):

constraints.statement: Confirm lifecycle signal at the realisation boundary. Design evidence states or points to upstream intent/requirement authority; build/realisation surface; assurance/proof surface; release/packaging posture; deployment/install posture; live-use/invocation posture; telemetry/projection/monitoring posture; retirement/revocation/supersession/decommission posture; and lifecycle-decision owner, source truth and authority boundary.

conditions: For each lifecycle phase.

grounding.quote:
The three are declared states of the
design evidence for a phase under that section, not result values; a
named gap is a residual

constraints.statement: Each phase is answered by active design/requirement/release/deployment/telemetry evidence, declared not applicable with reason, or recorded as a named Gap: or Unanswered: item with owning follow-up. A bare phase list is not design-method evidence. These are evidence states, not result values; a named gap persists as residual until its owning follow-up disposes it.

exceptions: A module may proceed with missing release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement truth only when the gap is explicitly governed.

grounding.quote:
Code, tests, generated artifacts or runtime fixtures may
confirm that a lifecycle claim is real, but they may not invent lifecycle
authority that the product, requirements, design, release or operational
surface did not declare (P6).

constraints.statement: Implementation proves a selected lifecycle path only within owned authority. Code, tests, artifacts and runtime fixtures may confirm claims but cannot invent undeclared lifecycle authority. Closure cannot rely on local convention, implementation precedent, mutable runtime state, prompt prose or test-only fixture behaviour.

exceptions: Verification-layer scenario changes are proposals pending Product-owner acceptance.

grounding.quote: superseded in its scenario-writing and scenario-failure sentences, proposed and pending the product owner's acceptance

constraints.statement: The proposed scenario change treats inability to write a capability scenario as unverified operational meaning requiring diagnosis, rather than proof the capability is unreal; scenario failure is observed-versus-expected disagreement, and actual-behaviour disagreement only with supported observation binding. Localisation may implicate realisation, governing claim, expected outcome or observation as evidence supports. C-11 closure on sign-off with unmet condition: EVALUATION §5 closes only by condition, reviewer result as input. C-12 findings only about tickets/columns/filenames: ACTIVATION §6 judges ambiguity removed and costs carrier findings as churn. All six are not run.

limitations: This is a source-linked interpretation proposal only. It performs no semantic acceptance, execution, qualification, release or completeness judgment.

The published STDO 2.5.1-rc.2 calculus is the workflow-selected basis. The candidate calculus described in these source sections is subject data, including its new laws and refusal choices; it does not replace that basis.

No tools, files, external sources or delegated work were used. External clauses, consumer loci, profile bindings, acceptance state and predecessor conservation claims remain unresolved where not supplied.

The output schema expresses operational definitions through concepts and constraints. Traversal, transformation and judgment populations remain uninstantiated and are preserved as empty by the adapter; descriptive records do not satisfy the subject's operational population law.

Exact field inventories, formulas, conditions and refusal boundaries are described, but this JSON is not an executable calculus model, exact source-record encoding, preservation witness or structural proof.

Source-disposition tables and the foundation consumer map are compacted into their substantive distinctions and explicit residuals; their external linked texts and full address-by-address resolution are not reproduced or verified.
The only deliberately omitted section is the heading-only application/import/exclusion parent. Its substantive children are retained separately.
Grounding quotes enable source re-entry; neither quotations nor processing dispositions establish whole-record fidelity or semantic completeness.
